# gitmoap_group_outbound (Data Source)

An organization's outbound policy. Each service's mode and the modes offered for it, whether the platform's public package registries are reachable without a rule, and every rule with when it last admitted a connection and what it allows that is easy to miss. Call it on the organization's top-level group; a subgroup's id is refused, naming its organization. Members who can view the organization's outbound settings may read it (Reporter and up).

The token needs `outbound:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_group_by_path" "acme" {
  full_path = "acme"
}

data "gitmoap_group_outbound" "acme" {
  group_id = data.gitmoap_group_by_path.acme.group_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_id` (String) The organization's top-level group

### Read-Only

- `platform_registries` (Boolean) Whether the public package registries the platform serves are reachable without a rule of
the organization's own.
- `published_version` (Number) The version your workloads are held to. Behind `version` for the moments after a change,
until the change reaches them.
- `rule_count` (Number) How many rules the organization holds.
- `rule_limit` (Number) The most rules the organization may hold.
- `rules` (Attributes List) The organization's rules, oldest first. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))
- `services` (Attributes List) Every service, with its mode and the modes offered for it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--services))
- `updated_at` (String) When it last changed; absent for an organization that never set one.
- `updated_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--updated_by))
- `version` (Number) The policy's version; every change advances it. Send it back with a change to refuse the
change if somebody else changed the policy since you read it.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Read-Only:

- `created_at` (String) When it was written.
- `created_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--created_by))
- `from_destination_id` (String) A destination an organization's code reached, counted per service, kind, port and decision
- `kind` (String) What a rule names.
- `last_admitted_at` (String) When it last admitted a connection, in the last 90 days.
- `note` (String) Why it exists.
- `ports` (List of Number) The ports it admits.
- `repository_ids` (List of String) The repositories whose workloads it applies to; every repository when empty.
- `rule_id` (String) An outbound rule: one destination an organization's code may reach
- `services` (List of String) The services it applies to; every service when empty.
- `updated_at` (String) When it last changed.
- `value` (String) The destination: a host name, `*.` and a domain, or an address or a range, in its ASCII
and canonical form.
- `warnings` (Attributes List) What it allows that is easy to miss. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--warnings))

<a id="nestedatt--rules--created_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.created_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `created_by_imported` (Attributes) An author who wrote on another host — a work item, a merge request, a comment, a release an import
brought — and whom nobody here is linked to yet. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--created_by--created_by_imported))
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor, and empty on a redacted one and on an outside author.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor and on an outside author (`imported`).
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.

<a id="nestedatt--rules--created_by--created_by_imported"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.created_by.created_by_imported`

Read-Only:

- `identity_id` (String) The outside author's id among the organization's imported identities.
- `login` (String) Their login on that host.
- `name` (String) Their name on that host, when it gave one.
- `profile_url` (String) Their profile's address on that host, when it gave one.
- `source_host` (String) The host they wrote on, such as `github.com`.



<a id="nestedatt--rules--warnings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.warnings`

Read-Only:

- `code` (String) What a rule's warning is about.
- `message` (String) The warning, in plain words.
- `suffix` (String) The shared-hosting suffix the rule's name falls under.



<a id="nestedatt--services"></a>
### Nested Schema for `services`

Read-Only:

- `available_modes` (List of String) The modes offered for the service where the organization runs. Choosing another is refused.
- `mode` (String) What a service's workloads may reach.
- `service` (String) A service that runs an organization's code. A new one joins by a new value here.
- `unavailable_reason` (String) Why a mode is not offered, when one is not.
